critique:
field pending_cubes, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Keep the field as the ordered list of [y, x] of highlighted cubes not yet picked up, written at the button-press step (the step whose execution steps list highlighted areas) and consumed at each pick-up step by removing the entry nearest the grasped cube's last table position. Change only the ordering key so the annotation is the same one the policy can compute: when writing the list at the button-press step, order the entries by increasing x (the robot's right-most cube first, left-most last). Across the minibatch the recorded pick order agrees with this key in every multi-cube episode but one, where the recorded order is a cyclic rotation of it (second-smallest x first, then third, then smallest); since no visible key explains that single case, annotate that episode by the same increasing-x rule so that the list and the policy's list are identical. Example: [[72, 126], [55, 145], [58, 163]].

field pending_cubes, POLICY PROMPT
  The clause 'in the order the areas are listed' sent the policy wrong at every button-press step with more than one highlighted area: the areas are printed sorted by y, while the recorded first entry was the right-most cube (smallest x). This breaks PREDICTABILITY: the policy wrote the list in printed order, the annotated memory held it in x-ascending order. Replace the clause with: 'When the execution steps shown at this step list highlighted-area positions, write one entry per area, the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area (as seen in that same execution step), and order the entries by increasing x, i.e. the robot's right-most cube first and the left-most cube last.' Keep the rest of the field unchanged: `[]` before the button press, remove the entry nearest the grasped cube's last table position at each step whose execution steps show a cube newly held (gripper down to ~0.02 height, fingers closing to ~46%), unchanged on a placing step. Example: [[107, 97], [116, 135], [80, 145]].

the policy prompt for subgoal
  Two changes. First, rule 3's pointing instruction on the button-press step currently says to point at the first entry of the list just written, so the pick target silently inherited the wrong ordering of the printed highlighted areas; state the ordering outright: on the button-press step, choose B and point at the highlighted cube with the smallest x among the cubes sitting on highlighted areas (the robot's right-most one), using its current position; at every later empty-gripper step, point at the first entry of the carried-in pending_cubes list (after removing any cube grasped on this step). Second, rule 3's phrase 'use the cube visible nearest the stored point' has no tolerance and broke SUFFICIENCY twice: after a placing, the gripper hovered at height ~0.15 directly above the next pending cube and hid it from the object list, so no cube was listed near the stored entry and the policy snapped to a different, unhighlighted cube 30-40 px away. Replace it with: 'Point at the visible cube that lies within about 15 px of the stored entry if there is one; if no listed cube is within that radius (the hovering gripper often hides the cube it is above), point at the stored entry itself, or at that cube's position in the most recent execution step where it was listed near the stored entry. Never redirect the point to a cube far from the stored entry or of a different colour from the one that was on the highlighted area.' Rules 1, 2, 4 and 5 stay as they are.
